title: Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin
capsule: The Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin was a hereditary monarchy on the Baltic coast of northern Germany, elevated from a duchy to a grand duchy at the Congress of Vienna in 1815 under Grand Duke Frederick Francis I. It was governed by the Mecklenburg House of Mecklenburg, one of Europe's oldest reigning dynasties, and maintained an anachronistically feudal constitution — the Estates constitution of 1755 persisted until 1918. The grand duchy joined the North German Confederation in 1867 and then the German Empire in 1871 as a constituent state, retaining its ruling house under Kaiser Wilhelm I. The monarchical order ended when Grand Duke Frederick Francis IV abdicated on 14 November 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The grand duchy's boundaries are well documented through nineteenth-century German cadastral and administrative sources, though its coastal and island boundaries with Prussia occasionally shifted.
